items.title: Proposed 31.4% French tax on regulated stablecoins could drive crypto traders offshore
items.summary: Chainalysis CEO in France Francois Volpoet warned the proposed 31.4% tax on regulated stablecoins could push traders toward unmonitored offshore channels.

items.title: Former FTX Europe chief targets U.S. tokenized stock trading with new SEC exemption
items.summary: Nasdaq-listed Perpetuals.com is the second company to pursue a U.S. tokenized stock marketplace under the SEC's new framework, following a joint venture between OKX and NYSE parent ICE.

items.title: Standard Chartered Will Hold Ripple's Stablecoin in Dubai—And Let Clients Trade With It Without Moving It
items.summary: The bank's Dubai branch now offers custody for Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin and plans a link with LMAX that lets institutions post it as trading collateral while the coins stay put.

items.title: Digital cash offers ‘cash-like privacy,’ but bank data breaches threaten users: BIS
items.summary: BIS said that digital cash can achieve “cash-like privacy,” however, the technology isn’t yet production-ready due to risks such as bank data breaches.

items.title: ENS seeks DAO approval to activate upgraded Ethereum naming system
items.summary: New .eth registrations would pause for hours during the transition, while existing domain holders could renew their names without migrating.

items.title: Qivalis wins Dutch e-money license for euro stablecoin
items.summary: Qivalis said the Electronic Money Institution authorization enables it to launch a euro-denominated stablecoin, with issuance planned for the coming months, subject to additional MiCA requirements.

items.title: How the SEC’s lack of leadership could facilitate crypto rulemaking
items.summary: A recent change in the SEC’s rules on quorum could make it easier for the agency to amend its approach to crypto regulation in the absence of a market structure bill.

items.title: Largest Philippines crypto exchange, Coins.ph, said to face central bank regulatory action
items.summary: The exchange, which has over 18 million customers, is said to have handled business transactions involving restricted offshore gaming and gambling companies.
